speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by clarifying the nature of that shooting pain: does it occur only when you touch or pressure the ear canal, or does it happen spontaneously as well? Also, since you mentioned difficulty wearing earrings, can you describe exactly where the discomfort is located?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pain when eating suggests possible nerve irritation; is the sensation sharp and radiating down your jaw, or is it a deep ache within the ear itself? Additionally, have you noticed any drainage, bleeding, or a feeling of fullness in the operated ear recently? REQUEST IMAGES: Otoscopy right ear.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal neuralgia (post-tympanoplasty) with granulation tissue irritation. The combination of shooting pain triggered by eating (jaw movement) and discomfort from earrings suggests nerve irritation alongside potential canal stenosis or granulation tissue from the recent surgery.
